report.summary: At 13:22 UTC, coredns was scaled down from 4 to 1 replica under a cost optimisation change (chg-8542). This reduction in capacity caused severe CPU saturation, high query latency, and error rate spikes starting at 13:23 UTC, followed by UDP read i/o timeout errors at 13:24 UTC. Consequently, notification-service experienced DNS resolution failures (getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN) starting at 13:25 UTC when attempting to reach external push and SMS vendors, leading to a 25% failure rate in notification deliveries.

ranked_hypotheses.title: CoreDNS replica scale-down causes DNS resolution timeouts for external vendors

supporting.note: Precedes symptom onset by 3 minutes and directly reduces coredns capacity.

Shows high DNS latency starting at 13:23.
Shows coredns error rate spike starting at 13:23.
Coredns logged UDP read i/o timeout errors starting at 13:24.
Shows the exact onset of the error surge at 13:25 UTC.
Indicates DNS getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN failures for push-provider starting at 13:25 UTC.
Indicates DNS getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN failures for sms-vendor starting at 13:25 UTC.
Past incident confirms coredns configuration/capacity issues cause similar EAI_AGAIN errors across services.

contradicting.note: Request rate remained stable, meaning the trigger was structural capacity reduction rather than a traffic spike.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External DNS or upstream resolver timeout coinciding with coredns replica change

supporting.note: Shows resolution errors specifically for push-provider.
Shows resolution errors specifically for sms-vendor.

contradicting.note: Proves internal coredns was severely resource-constrained at the exact same time.

The tight window after coredns change strongly points to the internal scaling change.
Simultaneous failure across two completely independent vendors points to a shared local resolver issue.

facts.text: notification-service depends synchronously on sms-vendor and push-provider, asynchronously on event-bus, and uses coredns for name resolution.
An infrastructure change chg-8542 scaled coredns replicas from 4 to 1 at 2026-10-14T13:22:00+00:00.
CoreDNS CPU percentage showed an anomaly starting at 13:23, peaking at 105.92% at 13:46.
CoreDNS latency p99 spiked upwards starting at 13:23, reaching a peak of 2112.52 ms.
CoreDNS error rate percentage showed an anomaly starting at 13:23, peaking at 22.72%.
CoreDNS logged UDP read i/o timeout errors starting at 13:24:03.
notification-service error rate metric spiked to 22.63% at 13:25:00 UTC and peaked at 26.58%
notification-service began logging DNS resolution errors for fcm.push-provider.example.com at 13:25:05 UTC
notification-service began logging DNS resolution errors for sms-vendor.example.net at 13:25:10 UTC

assumptions: Reducing coredns replicas from 4 to 1 left insufficient capacity to handle cluster DNS query load under normal operation.
Both external vendor DNS records experienced concurrent transient upstream resolution issues completely independent of the internal coredns resource saturation.

timeline.event: CoreDNS replicas scaled from 4 to 1 (cost optimisation)
CoreDNS CPU percentage, latency p99, and error rate anomalies begin
CoreDNS logs UDP read i/o timeout errors
notification-service logs getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN for push-provider
notification-service logs getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN for sms-vendor

recommended_actions.action: Scale coredns replicas back up from 1 to 4 to restore DNS query handling capacity.
recommended_actions.rationale: Directly mitigates the resource saturation and DNS lookup failures caused by chg-8542.

recommended_actions.action: Review cluster-wide core infrastructure cost-reduction changes and establish minimum replica thresholds.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents similar DNS or shared infrastructure bottlenecks from recurring during resource optimization efforts.
